intro: This is Storybound, a storybook for children from four to eight. A child draws a hero, and the app turns the drawing into a story that teaches a gentle lesson. The difference is that before any page reaches the child, an agent checks it against promises it wrote down first.
draw: The child draws right on the screen. Here is a bunny with a bow, and a carrot.
name: The child can name the hero, or let Pip, the helper, pick a name.
lesson: Next, a grown-up chooses the lesson. Here it is sharing. They can also add a promise of their own, for example: nobody in the story is left out.
making: Now the agent goes to work, and the screen shows what it is doing. It writes an oath: a list of promises for this drawing and this lesson. Then it writes each page and checks the page against every promise. A page that breaks a promise is rewritten before anyone sees it.
waiting: Pictures and a voice are made for every page as well. Nothing is shown to the child until everything for that page exists: the words, the picture and the narration. So this part takes a few minutes, and in the finished video we speed it up.
ready: The story is ready. The first page has its picture, and after a moment its voice starts reading it aloud by itself, so a small child never has to find a button. The Listen again button reads it once more, as often as they like.
choice_right: Every page ends with a choice. This one was the kind choice, and Pip celebrates it.
choice_wrong: A wrong answer is never a scolding. Pip explains gently and invites the child to try the other one.
pages: The rest of the story goes the same way. Each page was checked, and each has its words, its picture and its voice, ready before the child sees it.
quiz: After the story there is a short quiz. Every question was checked against the same promises, and a question that fails a check is dropped, never shown.
order: And a small game: put the pictures in the order they happened.
end: The story ends with a talk-about card, so a grown-up can chat about the lesson with the child.
receipt: Behind a grown-up gate, the parent gets the receipt. It says how many promises were checked, how many pages were rewritten, and which promises could not be fully kept. Nothing is hidden.
forget: And a parent can make the app forget the story, which deletes it from the server.
